security_audit.summary: Most static hits are Markdown examples or documentation for Localhero.ai commands and are false positives. Confirmed risks are scoped external CLI execution through npx, API key handling guidance, and third-party transfer of translation content; no prompt injection attempt was found.

remediation.suggestion: Keep allowed tools limited to npx @localheroai/cli commands and ask users before running commands that modify files or contact the service.
Prefer interactive login or user-managed environment variables. Do not ask users to paste API keys into prompts, logs, or shell commands.

remediation.issue: Translation content sent to an external service
remediation.suggestion: Tell users before source strings or translation files are sent to Localhero.ai, especially for private or regulated projects.

content.value_statement: Localization work can drift when source strings, glossary terms, and translation settings are handled separately. This skill guides agents through Localhero.ai workflows so teams can update i18n copy with fewer missed steps.
actual_capabilities: Reads localhero.json to identify the source locale and translation file paths.
Helps add or modify source-language i18n keys using existing project conventions.
Fetches glossary terms with the Localhero.ai CLI for consistent product language.
Fetches project tone, style, and language settings through the Localhero.ai CLI.
Runs changed-only translation generation when a Localhero.ai GitHub Action is not present.
Directs users to the Localhero.ai web UI for review, search, glossary, and settings tasks.
limitations: Requires a project configured with localhero.json and Localhero.ai translation files.
Requires authenticated Localhero.ai CLI access for glossary, settings, and translation commands.
Does not write target-language translations directly when Localhero.ai is expected to generate them.
May send source strings or translation files to Localhero.ai when CLI commands run.

use_cases.title: Add localized UI copy
use_cases.description: Create source-language keys for new screens while matching existing naming patterns and product tone.

use_cases.title: Keep terminology consistent
use_cases.description: Load glossary and style settings before editing user-facing strings for a feature or release.

use_cases.title: Prepare translation updates
use_cases.description: Run changed-only Localhero.ai translation generation or rely on the configured GitHub Action.

prompt_templates.title: Add a new source string
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner task for one UI label or message.
prompt_templates.prompt: Add a source-language i18n key for this new UI text: [text]. Follow the naming style in this project.

prompt_templates.title: Update feature copy
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate task for a small set of related strings.
prompt_templates.prompt: Update the source strings for [feature]. Check localhero.json, inspect existing keys, and keep the copy consistent with current conventions.

prompt_templates.title: Use glossary and settings
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate task where brand terms and tone matter.
prompt_templates.prompt: Before editing copy for [feature], fetch the Localhero.ai glossary and settings. Then update the source strings using those terms.

prompt_templates.title: Prepare a translation pull request
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced task that combines copy edits and translation generation.
prompt_templates.prompt: Add the needed source strings for [feature], check whether the Localhero.ai GitHub Action handles translations, and run changed-only translation generation if needed.

output_examples.input: Add copy for a new billing settings page.
output_examples.output: The assistant adds source-language keys for the page title, description, empty state, and primary actions. It follows the project key structure and requests translation generation only when needed.

output_examples.input: Refresh onboarding copy with approved product terms.
output_examples.output: The assistant checks glossary and style settings, updates the source strings, and notes which terms were applied for consistency.

output_examples.input: Prepare translations for changed checkout strings.
output_examples.output: The assistant checks for an existing Localhero.ai GitHub Action. If none is found, it uses the changed-only translation workflow and summarizes the affected files.

best_practices: Review localhero.json before editing any translation files.
Use glossary terms and project style settings before writing user-facing copy.
Ask before running Localhero.ai CLI commands that send data or modify files.
anti_patterns: Do not edit generated target-language files when Localhero.ai should manage translations.
Do not create new key naming styles without checking existing source files first.
Do not paste API keys into prompts, logs, or shared command transcripts.

faq.question: What does this skill help with?
faq.answer: It helps agents manage source-language i18n strings and Localhero.ai translation workflows in configured projects.

faq.question: Does it translate text directly?
faq.answer: No. The skill writes source-language strings and uses Localhero.ai workflows to generate or manage target translations.

faq.question: What configuration does it need?
faq.answer: It expects localhero.json and translation files that follow the project conventions.

faq.question: Does it use external commands?
faq.answer: Yes. It can run scoped npx @localheroai/cli commands for translation, glossary, settings, and login workflows.

faq.question: Can it work with GitHub Actions?
faq.answer: Yes. It checks whether a Localhero.ai GitHub Action will run translations automatically on a pull request.

faq.question: What should users review before running it?
faq.answer: Users should review authentication, sensitive source strings, and whether translation files can be sent to Localhero.ai.
